title: F#
subtitle: A functional-first language for .NET: immutable data, types that model the problem, pipelines of small functions, and full access to the .NET ecosystem.
description: F# (say "F sharp") is a functional-first, statically typed language that runs on .NET. It grew out of the ML family of languages, especially OCaml, and was created by Don Syme at Microsoft Research in Cambridge; its first release appeared in 2005. F# code is concise and expression-based, values are immutable by default, and the compiler infers almost every type, so programs read almost like scripts while keeping the safety of static types. It is used for financial modelling and trading systems, data analysis, scientific and engineering computation, domain-heavy business software, web services, and tooling, and it interoperates fully with C# and every .NET library.

This course is for anyone who has finished the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or has equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are, in any language. No previous functional programming is assumed. It goes from interactive scripts to functions and pipelines, records and discriminated unions, pattern matching, collections, options and results, type inference and units of measure, computation expressions and async code, interoperation with C#, and the tools F# developers use, ending with a complete program. It teaches F# 10 on .NET 10, the long-term-support release.

To run the examples, install the .NET 10 SDK from the [official download page](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download); F# is included. Save a program as `hello.fsx` and run it with `dotnet fsi hello.fsx`, or type `dotnet fsi` to explore interactively. There is no official online playground; the community's [Fable REPL](https://fable.io/repl/) runs F# in the browser by compiling it to JavaScript, which is fine for most short examples. Every complete program in these lessons was run with F# Interactive from the .NET 10 SDK, and the output shown is the output it printed.

levels.title: Thinking in expressions
levels.summary: Run scripts with F# Interactive, bind immutable values, write and compose functions, and model data with records, unions and pattern matching.

levels.title: Data, errors and types
levels.summary: Process data with lists, arrays, sequences, maps and sets; handle missing values and failures with options and results; and put type inference, generics and units of measure to work.

levels.title: F# in production
levels.summary: Use and build computation expressions for async and tasks, work hand in hand with C# and .NET libraries, and build, format and test a complete project.
